hook: Gold is so malleable a single ounce stretches 300 meters
fact: Gold atoms are so weakly bonded that one pound flattens into a sheet thin enough to read through. It never tarnishes.
subject: chemistry

hook: Rust is iron's slow burn — oxidation eating metal alive
fact: Iron reacts with oxygen gradually over years, creating iron oxide (rust). It's the same chemical as a fire, just slower.
subject: chemistry

hook: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes so violently it powers rockets
fact: H₂O₂ breaks down into H₂O + O₂ + heat. Military drones & WWII rockets used it as fuel due to the violent decomposition.
subject: chemistry

hook: Salt isn't a compound — it's a crystal lattice of ions
fact: NaCl forms a 3D grid where sodium & chloride ions alternate. Dissolving salt breaks these ionic bonds, allowing taste buds to detect it.
subject: chemistry

hook: Diamond & graphite are the same element but different structures
fact: Both are pure carbon, but arranged differently. Diamond's rigid 3D lattice makes it hardest substance. Graphite's layers slide — that's pencil lead.
subject: chemistry

hook: Water's high specific heat makes it Earth's temperature buffer
fact: Water absorbs huge energy changes with tiny temperature shifts. Oceans regulate climate; this is why coastal areas are temperate.
subject: chemistry

hook: Combustion is an exothermic redox reaction releasing light & heat
fact: Fire is fuel reacting with oxygen, producing CO₂, H₂O, & energy. It's rapid oxidation — same as rust, just explosive.
subject: chemistry

hook: Soap is a amphipathic molecule with split personalities
fact: One end loves water (hydrophilic), the other loves oil (lipophilic). Soap molecules trap oil, letting water wash it away.
subject: chemistry

hook: Catalysts speed reactions without being consumed
fact: Enzymes, catalytic converters, & industrial catalysts lower activation energy. They make reactions happen faster without being used up.
subject: chemistry

hook: Carbon can form 4 bonds simultaneously (that's why life exists)
fact: Carbon's 4 valence electrons allow infinite bonding patterns — chains, rings, 3D structures. Chemistry's versatility comes from this.
subject: chemistry

hook: pH is a logarithmic scale — pH 2 is 10× more acidic than pH 3
fact: Battery acid (pH 0) is a billion times more acidic than coffee (pH 5). One pH step = 10× change in hydrogen ion concentration.
subject: chemistry

hook: Bleach + ammonia creates toxic chloramine gas (deadly mix)
fact: Two common household cleaners react to form a poison that killed people who didn't know the danger. This is why warnings exist.
subject: chemistry

hook: Electroplating coats objects with metal using electricity
fact: Current forces metal ions to deposit onto an object. Your jewelry, car bumpers, & gold connectors are electroplated. Ancient Baghdad batteries did this.
subject: chemistry

hook: Polymer chains form plastics — same monomer, infinite arrangements
fact: Ethylene monomers link into polyethylene. Different structures = PET, PVC, PES. All plastics are just carbon chains in costumes.
subject: chemistry

hook: Fermentation is anaerobic respiration by bacteria & yeast
fact: Without oxygen, microbes convert glucose to ethanol (beer) or lactic acid (yogurt). Humans even ferment our muscles during intense exercise.
subject: chemistry

hook: Covalent bonds share electrons; ionic bonds steal them
fact: CO₂ is covalent (shared electrons). NaCl is ionic (sodium loses an electron to chlorine). Different structures = different properties.
subject: chemistry

hook: Osmosis is water molecules rushing toward salt through membranes
fact: Water moves from dilute to concentrated salt solutions to equalize concentration. Plant roots use this to absorb water from soil.
subject: chemistry

hook: Balancing equations is about counting atoms on both sides
fact: No atom is created or destroyed — only rearranged. H₂ + O₂ → H₂O means 2 H's + 1 O on each side must match.
subject: chemistry

hook: Esterification bonds fats to glycerin (why oils are greasy)
fact: Fat molecules have three ester bonds linking fatty acids to glycerol. Breaking these bonds makes soap — that's saponification.
subject: chemistry

hook: Equilibrium is reached when forward & reverse reactions balance
fact: In a reversible reaction, molecules form & break apart at equal rates. The amounts stop changing but reactions never stop.
subject: chemistry

hook: Sublimation skips the liquid phase (dry ice vanishes into air)
fact: CO₂ solid turns directly into gas. Frost also sublimates. Some solids have high enough vapor pressure to skip liquid entirely.
subject: chemistry

hook: Oxidation states track electron ownership during reactions
fact: An atom's oxidation state shows how many electrons it lost/gained. Fluorine always has -1; oxygen usually has -2. Helps predict reactions.
subject: chemistry

hook: Electronegativity is an atom's greed for electrons
fact: Fluorine is the greediest (4.0). Metals are generous. This difference creates polar bonds — unequal electron sharing.
subject: chemistry

hook: Activation energy is the barrier before a reaction ignites
fact: Wood won't burn below ~300°C even with oxygen present. That's activation energy. Once it ignites, heat keeps it going.
subject: chemistry

hook: Endothermic reactions absorb heat (ice cream melting is one)
fact: Some reactions need energy input to proceed. Melting, evaporation, & some reactions feel cold. Exothermic does the opposite.
subject: chemistry

hook: Molecular weight predicts how gas particles move
fact: Lighter gases diffuse faster. Hydrogen atoms outrun oxygen molecules. This is why perfume's smell spreads quickly — small molecules.
subject: chemistry

hook: Le Chatelier's principle: stress shifts equilibrium to resist change
fact: Increase pressure on a reaction? It shifts to reduce pressure. Add heat? It shifts to absorb heat. Systems fight back against stress.
subject: chemistry

hook: Chelation therapy traps heavy metals in organic cages
fact: Chelating agents wrap around lead, mercury, or iron — trapping them so kidneys can flush them out. Used to treat poisoning.
subject: chemistry

hook: Alloys are solutions where metals dissolve in metals
fact: Steel is iron + carbon dissolved together. Bronze is copper + tin. Mixing metals creates new properties — stronger, cheaper, smarter.
subject: chemistry

hook: Redox reactions transfer electrons between substances
fact: Oxidation loses electrons; reduction gains them. Rust, respiration, batteries — all redox. Remember: OIL RIG (Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain).
subject: chemistry
